MANAGER,
 BAJAJ ALLIANZ GENERAL INSURANCE  COMPANY LIMITED, VIVEKANANDA CORNER
entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text:
In this appeal, the petitioner has challenged the judgment dated 18.10.2010 passed in M.V.C.No.196/2006 by the Fast Track Court and Addl. MACT, Gadag, (for short, 'Tribunal').
2. The appellant was the petitioner and respondents were the respondents before the Tribunal.
For the sake of convenience, the rank of the parties will be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are, on 18.05.2006, at 10.30 p.m., while the petitioner was riding his cycle on Gadag-Laxmeshwar road near Kutir Hotel, auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-26/5066 driven in a rash and negligent manner and hit against the bicycle of the petitioner causing him injuries.
After taking treatment in the District Hospital, Gadag, the petitioner approached the Tribunal seeking compensation of Rs.4,00,000/- with interest at 18%.
The claim was opposed by the insurance company.

The Tribunal after recording the evidence and hearing both NC: 2024:KHC-D:7974 the parties, assessed the compensation of Rs.57,600/- with interest at 6% directing the owner of the auto rickshaw to pay the compensation.

Pleading inadequacy of compensation, seeking enhancement of compensation and also questioning fastening of liability against the first respondent, the petitioner has filed this appeal on various grounds.

4. Heard the arguments of Sri N.M. Patil, learned counsel for appellant and Smt. Anusha Sangami,
learned counsel for respondent No.2 and perused the records.
5.
It is the contention of the learned counsel for petitioner that the petitioner has placed evidence through PW-2 Dr. B.S. Patil assessing the whole body disability at 30%.
In spite of it, the Tribunal has taken the whole body disability only 7.5%.

The petitioner has suffered injuries all over the body including fracture of his right clavicle affecting the earning capacity and thereby the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is inadequate and sought for enhancement.

It is further contended that the NC: 2024:KHC-D:7974 Tribunal on the ground that the driver of the auto rickshaw was not holding valid driving licence and there is a violation of terms and conditions of the policy, held that the insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.
This aspect has been clarified by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Mukund Dewangan Vs.
Oriental
Insurance Company Limited1

. 
Learned counsel has also contended that the insurance company has collected extra premium and he sought direction to the insurance company to pay the compensation.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for insurance company has contended that the petitioner suffered clavicle fracture, which is an ornamental bone, no disability is caused affecting the earning capacity.

Sharanappa S/O Yamanappa @ Mudukappa ... vs Sri. Veerappa Channabasappa Bavikatti on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48406396/
2
In the evidence, the doctor has exorbitantly assessed the nature of injuries.

For an ornamental bone,
assessment of 7.5% disability is disproportionate and compensation assessed is on the higher side,
which needs to be reduced.
Learned (2017) 14 SCC 663 NC: 2024:KHC-D:7974 counsel did not dispute the principles laid down in Mukund Dewangan and he submits that the said principles may be adopted to this case.
7. I gave anxious consideration to the material evidence on record and perused the records.
8. The material on record point out that there was an accident between a cyclist/petitioner and the auto rickshaw on 08.05.2006 injuring him.
The petitioner has suffered fracture of clavicle and other injuries.
He was hospitalized for 13 days.

Since the petitioner was treated at Government Hospital,
there are no medical bills.
The petitioner was 19 years at the time of accident.
The Tribunal has awarded the compensation towards medical bills, loss of amenities and discomfort, attendant charges, traveling expenses, food and nourishment charges.

9. It is pertinent to note that the Tribunal did not award compensation towards pain and suffering,
loss of income during laid up period.
But assessed loss of earning NC: 2024:KHC-D:7974 capacity at Rs.48,600/-.

It is hard to accept the evidence of PW-2 that the petitioner has sustained 30%
disability.
The Tribunal is not correct in assessing the disability at 7.5% to the whole body.

Hence, in a case of this nature, the petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards pain and suffering, Rs.5,000/- towards medical expenses, Rs.2,000/- towards attendant charges, Rs.1,000/-
towards traveling expenses, Rs.3,000/- towards food and nourishment, Rs.10,000/- towards loss of amenities and discomfort and Rs.12,000/- towards loss of three months' income during laid up period, which comes to Rs.53,000/- and thereby the compensation assessed by the Tribunal at Rs.57,600/- is just compensation and accordingly, the petitioner is entitled.
Hence, it is not a case for enhancement of compensation.

10. As regarding the liability is concerned, on perusal of the impugned judgment, there is no specific finding that the insurance company has established that the driver of the auto rickshaw was not holding driving NC: 2024:KHC-D:7974 licence at the time of accident.
The Hon'ble Apex Court in Mukund Dewangan (supra) discussed about the liability on the part of the insurance company in a case of this nature.

This matter was also considered by the Larger Bench of the Hon'ble Apex Court in M/s. Bajaj Alliance General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Rambha Devi & others2 and Singh Ram Vs.
Nirmala and others3.

entities.text: M/s. Bajaj Alliance General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Rambha Devi & others2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text:
Singh Ram Vs.
Nirmala and others3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the law being settled, not holding of the valid driving licence at the time of accident is a breach of policy conditions.
Thereby the insurance company can avoid its liability but the principle of "pay and recovery" is applicable.
By applying the said principle, the insurance company has to deposit and then recover it from the insurer in the same proceedings.

Accordingly, the appeal merits consideration, in the result, the following:
ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed in part.

3 Civil Appeal No.841 of 2018 decided on 08.03.2022 Civil Appeal No.2103 of 2018, arising out of SLP  No.22630/2015, decided on 06.03.2018 NC: 2024:KHC-D:7974
(ii) The judgment and award dated 18.10.2010 passed in M.V.C.No.196/2006 by the Fast Track Court and Addl. MACT, Gadag, is modified.

(iii) The respondent-insurance company is  directed to pay the compensation of Rs.57,600/- along with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit, within eight weeks from the date of receipt of the copy of this judgment and recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle in the same proceedings.
(iv) Rest of the order of the Tribunal is kept intact.
